properties.name: A replayed gap is an ECHO — resolved by id, so mangling it can no longer re-key the answers
properties.rationale:
⭐ THE PROSE WAS DOING THE WORK THE CODE SHOULD HAVE DONE, which is why this is `defect_fix` and not `documentation`. The warning was loud, specific, correctly placed and read by both reporters — one of them trimmed the payload anyway, because trimming a large object for readability is what a well-behaved agent does. A warning that survives being read is not a control.

⚠️ AND THE FIX ALMOST CREATED THE DEFECT IT CLOSES. After the guard was corrected, both tool descriptions still carried the old warning — prose describing behaviour the code no longer has, which is instance ⑤'s exact shape (`fact:the-schema-described-the-answers-edge-for-months-before-it-existed`). Catching that took a deliberate second pass rather than the change itself. Recorded because it is evidence for `dec:idea-the-load-bearing-prose-is-unchecked-against-the-code-it-describes`: the same session that named the class was one edit from adding to it.

⚠️ WHAT THE SMOKE TEST TAUGHT WITHIN MINUTES: it acknowledged a gap and then phrased it, and the new refusal fired. The test's own assertion was "asking a gap records the question" — the acknowledged object was incidental — so the fix was to reorder the test, NOT to weaken the guard. Worth recording because the first instinct on a red gate is to soften the change that reddened it, and here that would have restored the defect.

⚠️ NOT CLOSED: storyflow's separate ask to name a `reason` on degrade needed no work — `degrade_reason` already exists, and the "payload differs" cause it would have named is now impossible. But the questions BOTH projects had recorded in degraded form are still sitting in their designs; correcting a Question's recorded wording remains open as `dec:idea-a-recorded-questions-wording-can-be-corrected`.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary:
`rehydrate_gaps` now resolves every replayed gap by `id` alone against a fresh `detect_gaps`, discarding whatever text the caller sends back. Implements the ECHO reading of `dec:idea-is-a-replayed-gap-an-input-or-an-echo`, settled by Anthony 2026-09-02.

THE GUARD WAS THE DEFECT, not the warning. It rehydrated ONLY when `description` and `evidence` were both empty — a row from a BUDGETED reply — so it trusted the caller's text in exactly the case where it can be wrong. Written for a different purpose, its condition asked "did the caller send nothing?" rather than "might what the caller sent be wrong?".

TWO PROJECTS, TEN DAYS APART, NEITHER CARELESS: dev_storyflow TRIMMED the description for readability (2026-08-23; 4 of 5 questions degraded to raw detector jargon and were RECORDED in that form under the user's name); proj:chama duplicated a fragment of the title while transcribing (2026-09-02). Two different mutilations, one silent re-key — which is the argument that the failure is the API's shape rather than carelessness, and what killed "the warning is enough" as an option.

BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, accepted with the ruling: a gap that is no longer open is REFUSED rather than served from a stale copy — INCLUDING AN ACKNOWLEDGED GAP. That is the point rather than a side effect: `acknowledge_gap` exists so a settled question is not re-asked, and phrasing one from a copy the server no longer recognises is exactly that re-ask. `gap_is_gone` now distinguishes "the gap is gone" from "your payload was wrong", which it previously conflated in one message that assumed the budgeted case.

TWO TESTS, THE FIRST WRITTEN TO FAIL. It mutilates the payload BOTH ways the field reports did — duplicated title and trimmed description — in a single call, and failed with exactly the field symptom (`rephrase_degraded: true`). The second pins the closed-gap refusal.

BOTH TOOL DESCRIPTIONS CORRECTED. The ⚠ "REPLAY EACH GAP OBJECT UNCHANGED ... trimming either for readability re-keys every answer" now describes behaviour the code does not have. They say the opposite, positively: the replay is an echo, and callers should NOT spend effort preserving it byte-for-byte.
